en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Chapter on Investigation 2.
The Question on the Prior Limit (Purimakoṭipañha)
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, regarding that which you say, 'the prior limit is not known,' please provide a simile for it.

"Great King, it is as if a man were to place a small seed in the earth; from that a sprout would emerge, and having gradually attained growth, development, and abundance, it would eventually yield fruit."
“Then, having taken that seed, one would plant it again; from that too a sprout would arise, which, gradually attaining growth, increase, and abundance, would yield fruit.
Is there, therefore, an end to this continuity?
“There is not, Bhante.”
“In the same way, Great King, the prior limit of the journey is not discerned.
“Give me a further simile.
“Suppose, Great King, there were a hen and an egg; from the egg comes the hen, and from the hen comes the egg.”
“Is there, therefore, an end to this continuity?
“No, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, the prior limit of this process of existence is not discerned.”
“Give me another simile,” he said.
The Elder drew a circle on the ground and addressed King Milinda thus:
“Great King, is there an end to this circle?”
“There is not, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, these wheels were spoken of by the Blessed One: ‘Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises;
the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, [craving].’”
“Craving; conditioned by craving, clinging; conditioned by clinging, kamma; from kamma, the eye arises again.
“Does this continuity, then, have an end?
“No, venerable sir.”
“Dependent on the ear and sounds … dependent on the mind and mental phenomena, mind-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; with contact as condition, feeling;
with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, kamma; from kamma—”
“Furthermore, the mind arises again.
“In this way, does there come to be an end to this continuity?
“There is not, Bhante.”
“In the same way, Great King, the prior limit of the journey is not discerned.
“You are clever, venerable Nāgasena,” he said.
This was the second question, concerning the prior limit.
